subject: AI Selloff Wipes $2.5T Off Nasdaq

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Data on tap:  The Oct. nonfarm payrolls report is due today, here's what to expect .

 AI trade fears:  Investors  are skeptical of Anthropic's ( ANT ) $1.5T IPO valuation .

 Financing risk:  Is Nvidia ( NVDA ) repeating Cisco's ( CSCO ) fatal dot-com playbook? 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 The reckoning 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
The AI trade faced a major reckoning on Thursday as a huge selloff wiped out $2.5T from the tech-heavy Nasdaq index. Notably, the index saw its worst intraday drop since the height of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020. While Nasdaq futures are up this morning, yesterday's selloff had far-reaching implications for the AI trade.

 Zoom in: The stock rout was fueled by the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, which prompted investor fears that data center construction could slow down. "The fundamentals surrounding the AI infrastructure buildout — or its potential pace — have been under fire due to questions around future funding, and the blue sweep just exacerbated that concern," said Nathan Peterson, director of derivatives research and strategy, Schwab Center for Financial Research. As a result, the Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) entered correction territory  and closed down 5.5% on Thursday. "Investors are pricing in power and funding bottlenecks, and the midterms added a political layer , as a new Congress will likely scrutinize data center permitting and power bills,” said Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen. “But Big Tech is a major Democratic donor, and falling tech stocks hit millions of retirement accounts. The more pressure builds, the more I expect Democrats to soften their stance."

 No dip-buying: Thursday also saw a notable change in trader behavior. Retail investors abandoned their signature dip-buying playbook to dump individual stocks at the fastest pace since March 2020. Shortly before market close, retail net outflows from single stocks reached $338M, Vanda Research noted. The selloff marked the third-largest day of retail single-stock liquidation on record, trailing only March 12 and March 17 of 2020. Vanda analyst Viraj Patel said institutional call buying slumped to a one-year low earlier in the week, while leveraged ETFs faced an estimated $42B-$48B in forced rebalancing into the close alongside de-risking from volatility-target funds. With institutional buyers stepping aside just as retail and systematic strategies aggressively unload equities, Patel warned that the collision represents flow dynamics rarely witnessed outside periods of acute market stress.

 Global rout: Asia was not immune to the selloff on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 index ( NKY:IND ) entering bear market territory  and ending below 60,000 for the first time since May. Tokyo-listed shares of investment giant SoftBank ( SFTBY ) sank nearly 11%, while those of memory chipmaker Kioxia ( KXIAY ) declined 8.7%.  South Korea's Kospi Index fell below the 5,000 level for the first time in nine months, before paring losses to end 6% lower.  Seoul-listed shares of SK Hynix ( SKHY ) and Samsung ( SSNLF ) slumped due to concerns over tighter U.S. regulation slowing AI investment and weakening memory chip demand, Saxo analysts said.  Taiwan's TAIEX index ( TWSE )  ended 4.5% lower, also entering bear market territory. TSMC ( TSM ), which accounts for over 40% of TAIEX's weighting, dropped 5% in Taiwan.  European markets also fell , tracking the tech selloff.
